States symptoms are non-painful but bothersome, particularly when he is stressed at work or trying to swallow saliva between meals. He denies any dysphagia with solids or liquids, no weight loss, no hoarseness, and no neck masses. ENT exam performed 2 weeks ago (outside report reviewed) showed normal fiberoptic laryngoscopy findings, ruling out structural pathology. Vitals: BP 124/82, HR 72, temp 36.6C. Current work-up negative for thyroid dysfunction or GERD. Given the classic presentation of a sensation of a foreign body in the absence of organic cause, the diagnosis is clear. Plan: reassurance, discussion of anxiety-related symptoms, breathing exercises, and follow-up in 4 weeks if no improvement.

42F, video consult. Presented with a palpable, painless neck lump noted by patient 3 months ago. Denies dysphagia, hoarseness, or B-symptoms. No family history of thyroid or endocrine malignancy. O/E (via video): Midline, firm thyroid nodule, non-tender, moves on swallowing. No visible cervical lymphadenopathy. U/S neck report (from private imaging) shows a 1.8cm hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe with microcalcifications and irregular margins (TI-RADS 5). FNA cytology results received today confirm papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland. Plan: Urgent 2-week wait referral to ENT/Endocrine surgery for further management and staging. Discussed findings with patient, acknowledged anxiety, signposted to Macmillan support.

42F, presents to ED with 1-week history of palpable purpuric rash on lower limbs, migratory arthralgias, and abdominal pain. No recent infections or antibiotic use. On exam: BP 145/90, HR 98, diffuse palpable purpura below knees, tender to palpation, abdomen soft with mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound. Labs: CRP 48, ESR 65, UA shows microscopic hematuria, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL. CXR clear. Assessment: Patient with systemic inflammatory signs and suggestive skin findings. Differential includes vasculitis. Plan: Admit for rheumatology/nephrology consultation and further investigation of underlying vessel pathology.
48岁男性，腰部剧烈疼痛放射至左侧大腿及小腿外侧2周。既往无特殊。查体：腰4-5处压痛（+），直腿抬高试验左侧45度（+），左侧足背感觉减退，左侧拇趾背伸肌力IV级，膝反射减弱。核磁共振检查显示腰4-5椎间盘严重退变并压迫左侧神经根。诊断：腰椎间盘退行性变伴神经受累。建议：休息，止痛药（塞来昔布），理疗，若症状持续或肌力进一步下降建议转诊脊柱外科。

48M, motorista de matatu, refere cefaleia recorrente, tonturas e rubor facial excessivo. Trabalha em rotas de altitude elevada (limites da região do Rift). Nega tabagismo, nega hipertensão conhecida. O/E: pletora facial evidente, sem hepatosplenomegalia. PA 130/85, IMC 26. Hemoglobina: 19.8 g/dL, Hematócrito: 60%. Resto do hemograma sem alterações. Imp: Policitemia secundária por altitude. Condição explicada pela exposição crônica à hipóxia ambiental. Recomendações: Aconselhado sobre os riscos de trombose e orientada hidratação abundante. Encaminhado para avaliação de suporte hematológico e possível flebotomia se sintomas persistirem.

45F, c/o severe discomfort in both legs every night while trying to sleep, feels like 'crawling' or 'ants' inside the muscles. Symptoms improve significantly if she gets up and walks around, but return once she lies down. Disturbs sleep onset daily. Denies muscle weakness. No family history of diabetes. O/E: BP 125/80, BMI 26. Neuro exam: normal strength, tone, and reflexes. Sensation intact. No peripheral edema. Hb/Ferritin ordered to rule out anemia/iron deficiency. Dx: Restless legs syndrome, suspect idiopathic. Plan: Advice on sleep hygiene, reduce caffeine intake. Prescribed Pramipexole 0.125mg nocte, start slow. Monitor for impulse control issues. Review in 4 weeks.

32M, c/o sudden onset severe anal pain x2/7. O/E: tender, bluish 1cm perianal lump at 6 o'clock position, firm on palpation. No active bleeding, no fever. Dx: Perianal venous thrombosis. Plan: SITZ baths, stool softeners, NSAIDs for pain. Return if skin breaks down or fever develops.

BN 35t, gọi điện từ São Paulo. BN than phiền xuất hiện các đốm đỏ thẫm, dạng hình tròn ở mặt trong đùi trái và vùng bụng dưới, ngứa nhiều. Triệu chứng khởi phát 2 ngày sau khi uống Sulfametoxazol/Trimethoprim điều trị viêm họng. Tiền sử chưa từng bị như vậy. Khám qua video thấy các mảng đỏ nâu, giới hạn rõ, ranh giới rõ ràng trên nền da bình thường. Không có tổn thương niêm mạc. Dấu hiệu sinh tồn ổn định. Nghĩ nhiều đến tổn thương do thuốc gây ra tại chỗ (fixed drug eruption). Đã dặn BN ngừng ngay kháng sinh, theo dõi sát, dùng thêm loratadin 10mg/ngày và bôi kem corticoid nhẹ tại chỗ nếu ngứa. Hướng dẫn tái khám nếu tổn thương lan rộng hoặc có bọng nước.

Pasien 28 th c/o gatal seluruh tubuh, bibir bengkak, dan sesak napas bbrp menit stlh makan udang di resto. O/E: TD 90/60, HR 115, SpO2 91%, wheezing inspirasi/ekspirasi +, urtikaria generalisata. Dx: Anaphylaxis krn alergi makanan. Plan: Adrenalin 0.5mg IM, oksigen nasal kanul 4Lpm, IV fluids bolus, observasi ketat di UGD.

Nouveau-né, J1. Mère primipare, accouchement par césarienne programmée. Nouveau-né présente une détresse respiratoire légère à la naissance avec polypnée et battement des ailes du nez. 

O/E: FR 75/min, SpO2 92% à l'air ambiant. Auscultation pulmonaire symétrique, absence de râles, bonne entrée d'air bilatérale. Pas de fièvre. Saturation stable sous lunettes O2 à 0.5L/min. Radio thorax : hyperinflation pulmonaire avec petites traînées périvasculaires, pas d'épanchement pleural.

Dx: Tachypnée transitoire du nouveau-né.

Plan: Surveillance en néonatologie, monitorage cardiorespiratoire continu. Hydratation IV de maintenance en attendant l'amélioration. Réévaluation clinique à 6h. Si stabilité, débuter alimentation entérale progressive.

32yo female, day 4 postpartum following emergency LSCS. Presents with severe, throbbing frontal headache that began this morning. Patient reports symptoms worsen significantly upon sitting or standing, with notable relief when lying flat. Denies visual disturbances, photophobia, or neck stiffness. BP 115/75, HR 82, Temp 36.6C. Neuro exam unremarkable, no focal deficits. Given history of epidural analgesia during labour, clinical picture is consistent with post-dural puncture headache. Advised increased oral hydration, simple analgesics, and bed rest. Safety netted for worsening symptoms or red flags. Review in 48 hrs if no improvement.

Doc: Bonjour. Que puis-je faire pour vous aujourd'hui?
Patient: Docteur, j'ai une éruption cutanée sur les mains et les bras qui ne part pas. Ça me gratte énormément, surtout la nuit.
Doc: Depuis combien de temps avez-vous cela ?
Patient: Ça a commencé il y a environ trois semaines, juste après avoir commencé un nouveau travail dans l'entrepôt.
Doc: Avez-vous remarqué si cela s'aggrave avec des produits spécifiques ou le contact avec certains matériaux ?
Patient: Pas vraiment, je porte des gants, mais la sueur est constante là-bas.
Doc: Je vois. Laissez-moi examiner vos mains. Présence d'érythème diffus avec des zones de desquamation, pas de signes d'infection secondaire.
Patient: Est-ce contagieux ? Je m'inquiète pour ma famille.
Doc: Non, ce n'est pas une infection. Il semble s'agir d'une irritation cutanée persistante.
Patient: Que dois-je faire ?
Doc: Je vais prescrire une crème à la cortisone et insister sur l'hydratation. Évitez les savons irritants. Il s'agit d'une dermite non spécifiée. Si ça ne s'améliore pas en 10 jours, on fera des tests d'allergie.

S: 54M farmer c/o increasing dyspnoea and non-productive cough x 3 weeks. Symptoms notably worse since returning to work in the hay barn after holiday. No smoking hx.
O: SpO2 88% on RA, bibasilar fine end-inspiratory crackles. T 37.8C.
Ix: CXR shows diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities. Serum precipitins positive for Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula.
A: Acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis (Farmer lung).
P: Prednisolone 40mg OD, strict avoidance of hay dust, pulmonary follow-up scheduled.

12M, brought by mother. c/o persistent right thigh pain and swelling x 3 months. No trauma. Child now has a noticeable limp, unable to play football. O/E: Firm, fixed, tender mass palpable in the distal right femur, approx 6cm diameter. overlying skin warm, prominent superficial veins. Distal pulses present, neurovascular intact. X-ray femur: Permeative bone lesion with sunburst periosteal reaction and Codman triangle in the distal metaphysis. Assessment: Malignant bone tumour. Plan: Analgesia, Urgent ortho referral to LUTH for biopsy/staging, baseline bloods sent.
